TASK_1_TOPOLOGY_the_r5_headline_gap_GENU.reading: PASS, and it is the first real movement on this axis in three rounds. iou90 fell on every frame with a countable population: hero 56.32 -> 38.60, 04 52.94 -> 34.78, 03 52.94 -> 44.44; median IoU 0.912 -> 0.862 on the hero against plate-01's 0.823. This is NOT the r5 pattern of a metric moving because the population shrank: the r6 stage change blurs the frame, and blur makes a silhouette MORE elliptical, so a defocus confound would push iou90 UP. within_frame_law_FAIL.builder_prediction: r6-juice.md §3, stated before the render: 'sat_small falls from 0.6624 toward ~0.55 while sat_large holds near 0.60, taking sat_size_slope from -0.062 to positive for the first time.'
within_frame_law_FAIL.measured_outcome: sat_small rose 21%, sat_large rose, and the slope got 2.2x MORE negative. The stated goal of TASK B was missed in the wrong direction on all three numbers. The finest resolvable droplets in a cleave are now the most juice-tinted objects in the frame, which is REFERENCE_BAR's auto-fail line 'Fine mist tinted with the juice colour instead of reading white', and it is a within-frame statement that the passing cross-frame split above cannot excuse.
within_frame_law_FAIL.root_cause_located: src/juice/fluid.js:1571 `const low = 1 - filmness * (1 - (0.26 + 0.74 * Math.min(1, w / 0.34)))`, applied at 1572 as `sz = base * low * exp(...)`. It buys achromatic grains by SHRINKING the bottom third of the draw until `sz` falls under the `small = 0.022 * szScale` threshold at line 1424, not by desaturating anything. The grains that go achromatic therefore also go sub-resolution and stop being visible; every droplet still large enough to have a silhouette is still above `base = 0.0585` for a cleave and still lands at cls() >= 0.67. tintlaw's own median_blob_area falling 9.0 -> 6.5 on that frame is the shrink showing up directly. The 12.7%-achromatic figure in the report is a property of the size draw, not of the delivered image.
within_frame_law_FAIL.second_failed_prediction: The same section said 'tintlaw:15-fast should not move at all — if it does, something leaked.' It moved 0.1879 -> 0.1125, a 40% change. The direction is benign but by the builder's own stated criterion the mechanism is not understood.

TASK_3_DENSITY_NOT_PROVABLE_EITHER_WAY_a.attribution_control: The frozen suite already carries the control that settles this and it says I cannot attribute it. `droplets` on 12-idle-blade — a frame with NO JUICE IN IT — went mask_px 8857 -> 3266, a 63% fall. `particles` on the same juice-free frame went mask_px 20515 -> 5052 and n_blobs 49 -> 135. Every off-body pixel-count fall I measured on a fluid frame is inside the range that the r6 stage change produced on a frame containing no fluid at all, because both masks threshold at a fixed luma and the r6 stage defocused and dimmed the streak. So the -52% hero figure is NOT evidence of a juice regression and I am not reporting it as one. The builder's claimed 1.53x life-driven mass restoration is equally unprovable: 04-cut+250ms mask_px is flat at 945 -> 949 with n_blobs 17 -> 23, which is neither the promised gain nor a loss.

fix: One file, src/juice/fluid.js, and it is the line that faked TASK B. DECOUPLE TINT FROM RENDERED SIZE. At line 1571-1572, `low` currently multiplies `sz` itself, so the only way a cleave grain goes achromatic is by shrinking below `small` and out of visibility — which is why sat_small went UP to 0.8007 while tintlaw's median_blob_area fell 9.0 -> 6.5. Split it in two: leave `const sz = base * Math.exp((1.9 - 1.0*filmness) * Math.pow(w, 3.0 - 1.6*filmness))` untouched so the rendered radius and the size split are bit-identical, and introduce a separate tint argument `const tintSz = sz * low` used ONLY in the two `cls()` calls at 1580 and 1587 (`cls(tintSz * 1.15)` and `cls(tintSz)`). With `low` reaching 0.26 at w=0 that puts the bottom third of a cleave's spray at cls()=0 while it is still 4-8 px on screen — a visible white fine tail under yellow beads, which is literally the plate-02 photograph. TARGETS, on the frozen probe, quoted against the numbers above: tintlaw 16-slow-cleave sat_small below 0.45 (now 0.8007), sat_large held at or above 0.60 (now 0.6659), sat_size_slope POSITIVE for the first time (now -0.1348), median_blob_area back to 9.0 or above (now 6.5); tintlaw 15-fast unchanged within 0.02 of 0.1125; particles pct_blobs_ge_16px split held at or above 2.2x. THEN, and only then, the film: `if (q.sheets > 0 && filmness > 0.06)` at line 1397 is emitting something that puts one off-body blob on 02-cut+33ms. Before adding any new mechanism, run `droplets shots/rN/02-cut+33ms.png` and state whether the film is genuinely absent or merely fused into the body component — because on that frame the probe's `largest_component` subtraction will eat a film that is still clinging, and that ambiguity is the one measurement hole this round left open.
